explanation: The correct match is as follows- My Presidential Years – R. Venkataraman The Hindu View of Life – S. Radhakrishnan Voice of Conscience – V. V. Giri Without Fear of Favour – N. Sanjiva Reddy 47.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · Modern India GS p.334

subject: AP & Indian History
topic: Advent of Europeans & East India Company
question: Which part of India remained under Portuguese control even after August 15, 1947?
explanation: India got independence on August 15, 1947 but Goa remained under Portuguese control even after independence. Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule on December 19, 1961. It was a part of Union Territory of Goa, Daman & Diu till 30th May 1987 when it was carved out to form a separate state. 3. Consider the following statements: 1. Asaf Ali looked after the work of Railway Ministry in the Interim Government (1946) 2. 'Ancient Monuments Preservation Act' was passed when Lord Curzon was Governor General. 3. The Haripura Session of the Indian National Congress was presided over by C.R. Das.
source: MPPSC (Pre) G.S. 2010 · Modern India GS p.335

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Swami Shraddhanand suggested no-tax campaign as a protest against the Rowlatt Act. History of Modern India 33 Miscellaneous Of these statements:
explanation: In the Interim Government of 1946, Railway and Transport Portfolio was headed by Asaf Ali. The Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904 was passed on March 18, 1904 by British India during the regime of Lord Curzon . The Indian National Congress met at Haripura during February 19 to 22, 1938, under the Presidency of Subhas Chandra Bose. He was elected President of the Haripura Congress Session (51th Session) in 1938. The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crime Act (1919) popularly known as Rowlatt Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council of British India in March, 1919. The Act provided the authority to the British government to arrest and imprison suspects without trial. In protest to this Act, Swami Shraddhananda suggested starting the movement of not paying rent (Lagaan).
source: UP Lower (Pre) G.S. 2013 · Modern India GS p.335

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange the following incidents in chronological order. (i) Cripps Mission (ii) Mountbatten Plan (iii) Quit India Movement (iv) Home Rule League
explanation: • Home Rule League was launched by Annie Besant in September 1916 at Madras. • The Cripps Mission was a failed attempt in late March 1942 by the British government to secure full Indian cooperation and support for their efforts in World War II. • The Quit India Movement was a movement launched at the Bombay session of all India Congress Committee by Gandhi on 8 August 1942. • Mountbatten Plan was proposed in May 1947 by Lord Mountbatten. The plan was put into action by the Indian Independence Act, 1947 which was to be partitioned into two dominions- India and Pakistan.
source: Gujarat PSC Pre-2019 Paper-I · Modern India GS p.335

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following two places in Mumbai had Salt Markets during the British time?
explanation: Bhendi Bazar and Wadala were the two places in Mumbai that had Salt Markets during the British time.
source: Maharashtra PSC 2022 · Modern India GS p.336

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Arrange the following Acts in their chronological order and select the correct answer from the code given below: I. Lex - Loci Act II. Bengal Tenancy Act III. Age of Consent Act IV. Indian University Act History of Modern India 33 Code −−−−
explanation: The Act in their chronological order as follows - Lex - Loci Act 1850 Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 Age of Consent Act 1891 Indian University Act
source: UPPCS RO/ARO (Pre) 2023 (Cancelled) · Modern India GS p.336

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which statement is true regarding Bipin Chandra Pal? 1. He was a Brahmo Samaj Leader and Social Reformer. 2. A weekly magazine named New India was published. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code −−−−
explanation: Bipin Chandra Pal was an Indian nationalist and freedom fighter. He was associated with Brahmo Samaj. He worked as writer, orator, social reformer. As a journalist, Pal worked for Bengal Public opinion, the Tribune and New India. Hence both statements are correct.
source: UPPCS RO/ARO (Pre) 2023 (Cancelled) · Modern India GS p.336

subject: AP & Indian History
question: For whom did K.M. Panikkar say that "He was the first diplomat of modern India"?
explanation: K.M. Panikkar attributed Dadabhai Naoroji that he "was the first diplomat of modern India".
source: MPPSC (Pre) 2024 23/06/2024 · Modern India GS p.336

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following pairs: Party Its Leader 1. Bharatiya Jana Dr. Shyama Prasad Sangh Mukherjee 2. Socialist Party C. Rajagopalachari 3. Congress for Jagjivan Ram Democracy 4. Swatantra Party Acharya Narendra Dev How many of the above are correctly matched?
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- Party - It's Leader Bhartiya Janasnagh - Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Socialist Party - Acharya Narendra Dev Congress for Democracy - Jagjivan Ram Swatantra Party - C. Rajagopalachari Hence, pairs 1 & 3 are correctly matched.
source: UPSC IAS (Pre.) 2024 · Modern India GS p.336

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following is wrongly matched regarding 'Praja Mandals'?
explanation: Balwant Rai Mehta established Praja Mandal at Bhavnagar in Gujarat (not in Madhya Pradesh). Hence, pair (b) is incorrectly matched.
source: APPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.337

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following events pertaining to the Freedom Movement of India: (i) Mountbatten Plan (ii) Quit India Movement (iii) Wavell plan (iv) Royal Indian navy Mutiny Select the correct chronological order of these events using the codes given below.
explanation: The correct chronological order of events pertaining to the freedom movement of India as - Quit India Movement (1942), Wavell Plan (1945), Royal India Navy Mutiny (1946) and Mountbatten Plan (1947).
source: ASSAM PSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.337

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements about Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel: (i) He got the moniker 'Sardar' due to his organizational skills during Bardoli Satyagraha. History of Modern India 34 (ii) The Prison where Mahatma Gandhi and Sardar were cellmates was Naini Prison. (iii) He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1989. (iv) He was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India. Select the incorrect statements using the codes given below.
explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was a prominent figure in the Indian freedom struggle who later became first Deputy Prime Minister and first Home Minister of India. He got the Moniker 'Sardar' due to his organisational skills during Bardoli Satayagraha. He and Mahatma Gandhi were cell-mates in Yerawada prison (Not in Naini Prison) after the arrestment in 1932 due to failure by 2nd Round Table Conference. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1991 (Not in 1989). Hence, only statements I & IV are correct.
source: ASSAM PSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.337

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statement on the contributions of Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar: I. His great contribution was for the uplifment of women in India. II. He organized a powerful movement for the enactment of Widow Remarriage Act. III. To propagate his social ideas, he published Sambad Kaumudi, a Bengali weekly newspaper. Which of the above statement are correct?
explanation: Pandit Iswar Chandra Vidyasagar was a nineteenth centrury polymath reformer, whose contribution towards the upliftment of women in India is remarkable. Hence statement -I is correct. He organised a powerful movement as a result, Government of India passed the Widow Remarriage Act in 1856. Hence statement-II is also correct. Sambad Kaumudi, was a weekly newspaper published by Raja RamMohan Roy (not by Iswar Chandra Vidyasagar). The newspaper actively compaigned for the abolition of sati pratha. Hence statement-III is not correct.
source: APPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.337

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following events: I. Swadeshi Movement II. Surat Split III. Lucknow Pact IV. Home Rule Movement Which of the above main events took place during the extremist phase?
explanation: The extremist phase was started in 1905 and ended in 1918. In this phase Swadeshi Movement, Surat split, Lucknow pact and Home Rule Movement took place.
source: APPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.338

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following events: I. Visit of Simon Commission to India II. Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore session III. Launch of Dandi March Which of the above main events took place during the tenure of Lord Irwin?
explanation: Lord Irwin was the viceroy of British India from 1926 to 1931. During the tenure of Lord Irwin events like visit of Simon Commission in India, (1927), Purna Swaraj Resolution at Lahore session (1929) and Dandi March (1930) took place.
source: APPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.338

subject: AP & Indian History
question: After passing away of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, who from the followers of Dr. Ambedkar, became member of the Congress ? (A) R.D. Bhandare (B) Rajabhau Bhole (C) Dadasaheb Rupwate (D) Bapusaheb Rajbhoj
explanation: R. D. Bhandare was a member of the Indian National Congress political party and also he was twice elected to Lok Sabha. Dadasahab Rupwate was member of the Scheduled Caste Fedration and the Republician Party of India and later the Indian National congress. Rajaram Ramji Bhole was an Indian politican and follower of Dr. Amberdkar became a member of The Indian National Congress. Bapusaheb Rajbhoj was not a follower of Dr. Ambedkar, he became a member of The Congress Party and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the then Congress government.
source: Maharashtra PSC 2022 · Modern India GS p.338

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the Architect of Mumbai's ‘Gateway of India’?
explanation: The Gateway of India was designed by the British architect, George Wittet.
source: UPPSC APO 2022 · Modern India GS p.339

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Ambabai, a woman freedom fighter, belonged to which of the following States of India?
explanation: Ambabai was a woman freedom fighter, who belonged to state of Karnataka.
source: 69th BPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.339

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following events during India’s Freedom Struggle : 1. Home Rule Movement 2. Surat Split 3. Kheda Satyagraha 4. Minto-Morley Reforms Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the events given above?
explanation: The correct chronological order of freedom struggle is as - Surat Split (1907), Minto-Morley Re Form (1909), Home rule movement (1916) and Kheda Satyagraha (1918).
source: 69th BPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.339

question: Match List-I with List-II : List-I (Explorer) List-II (Birthplace) A. Christopher 1. Portugal Columbus B. Jacques Cartier 2. United Kingdom C. Sir Francis Drake 3. Italy D. Ferdinand Magellan 4. France Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
explanation: The correct match is as follows :- List-I List-II (Explorer) (Birthplace) Christopher Columbus – Italy Jacques Cartier – France Sir Francist Drake – United Kingdom Fredinand Magellan – Portugal
source: 69th BPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.339

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the statements regarding the nationalist Romesh Chunder Dutt. (1) He translated Ramayana and Mahabharata. (2) He was president of the Indian National Congress. (3) He qualified the ICS. (4) He was president of the Bangiya Sahitya Parishad. Which of the following statements are correct?
explanation: Romesh Chunder Dutt was an Indian Civil Servant, economic historian. He translated Ramayana and Mahabharta. He was also first president of Bangiya Sahitya Parishad is a literary society of Kolkata, West Bengal, which aims to promote Bengali literature. He also became President of Indian National Congress in 1899. Hence, all statements are correct.
source: Odisha PSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.340

subject: AP & Indian History
question: "This diamond of India, this jewel of Maharshtra, this prince of workers…….. . Look at him and try to emulate him," Who made this remark about Gopal Krishna Gokhale?
explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak praised Gopal Krishna Gokhale during the funeral of Gokhale as the Diamond of India, the Jewel of Maharashtra and the prince of workers.
source: TSPSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.340

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which of the following decision was taken by Sabarmati treaty?
options: A competitive co-operative party should be established.
Students should not be involved in politics.
There should be ho discrimination among lower caste workers and a team of 50 volunteers should be formed and Hindu Muslim unity should be maintained.
A committee of Motilal Nehru and Jayakar to determine the members of the Central Legislature.
explanation: In Sabarmati Pact, 1926, A committee under Motilal Nehru and Jayakar formed to determined the members of the Central Legislature.
source: MH PSC (Pre) 2023 · Modern India GS p.340

question: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? List I (Period) List II (Wars) 1. 1767-69 AD First Anglo-Maratha War 2. 1790-92 AD Third Anglo-Mysore War 3. 1824-26 AD First Anglo-Burmese War 4. 1845-46 AD Second Anglo-Sikh War Select the correct answer using the codes given below
explanation: The First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-82 AD) was the first among the three Anglo-Maratha wars fought between the British and Maratha empire in India. The war began with the Treaty of Surat (1775 AD) and ended with the Treaty of Salbai (1782 AD). The Third Anglo-Mysore War was fought during 1790-92 AD between the British and Tipu Sultan and ended with the Treaty of Srirangapatanam. The Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26 AD) was the first in the series of wars that were fought between British India and Burma. The prolonged war ended with a decisive victory of the British and the famous “Treaty of Yandabo”(1826 AD) was signed. The Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49 AD) was fought between the Sikh empire and the British East India Company. The Battle at Ramnagar was indecisive whereas the Sikhs won at Chilianwala. The final battle was fought at Gujarat near river Chenab (not the present Indian state Gujarat) in 1849 AD. It was won by the British forces. Punjab was annexed by the British in March 1849 AD (under Lord Dalhousie) under the ‘Treaty of Lahore’. The eleven year-old Maharaja, Duleep Singh was pensioned off to England.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2004 · Modern India GS p.343

question: The Anglo-Afghan relations in the 19th century was influenced by the fear of expansion towards India of-
explanation: In the late 19th century the East India Company became worried about Russia. It anticipated that Russia might expand across Asia and enter India from the north-west. Driven by this fear, the British now wanted to secure their control over the north-west. Hence they fought a prolonged war with Afghanistan between 1838 AD and 1842 AD and established Company’s indirect rule there. Sind was taken over in 1843 AD. Next in line was Punjab. But the presence of Maharaja Ranjit Singh held back the Company. After his death in 1839, two prolonged wars were fought with the Sikh kingdom. Ultimately, in 1849 Punjab was annexed. The fear of Russian expansion during 19th century was the base of Anglo-Afghan war.
source: UPPCS (Mains) Spl. G.S. 2004 · Modern India GS p.346

question: What is true for Planning in India? 1. In August 1937, the Congress Working Committee at its meeting in Wardha adopted a resolution of national reconstruction and social planning. 2. Subhash Chandra Bose, in his presidential speech at Haripura declared that the national state on the advice of planning commission would adopt a comprehensive scheme. 3. Modi Government renamed 'Planning Commission' as 'Niti Aayog'. 4. Subhas Chandra Bose announced the formation of a National Planning Committee with Jawaharlal Nehru as Chairman in 1938.
explanation: The 51st session of the Indian National Congress was held in the year 1938 at Haripura village in Surat. Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose presided over this session. In his presidential address to the Haripura session, Bose said that through the ‘Planning Commission’ more states would accept comprehensive policies. In 1938 Formation of National Planning Committee, under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru was also announced to be set up. It is noteworthy that proposal for national reconstruction and social planning was accepted by the Congress Working Committee in the Wardha Meeting in August 1937. The Planning Commission was constituted on 15th March, 1950 on the recommendation of the K.C. Niyogi Committee as a non-constitutional, advisory body. On 1st January, 2015 the Modi government established NITI Aayog in place of the Planning Commission. It is clear that all the statements in question are true. Hence, option (b) will be the correct answer.

question: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the battle fought in India in the 18th Century?
options: Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Buxar – Battle of Ambur – Battle of Plassey
Battle of Ambur – Battle of Plassey – Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Buxar
Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Plassey – Battle of Ambur – Battle of Buxar
Battle of Ambur – Battle of Buxar – Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Plassey
explanation: The correct chronological order of the battles fought in India during 18th century is as follows- Battle of Ambur – Battle of Plassey – Battle of Wandiwash – Battle of Buxar. The Battle of Ambur was the first battle of the Second Carnatic War fought in 1749 between Anwar-ud-Din, the incumbent Nawab of the Carnatic and an allied army formed by the new Nizam of Hyderabad, the French, and a claimant to the Nawabship of the Carnatic. The Battle of Plassey took place on June 23, 1757 between the forces of the East India Company, led by Robert Clive (Clive of India) and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daula. The Battle of Wandiwash was fought in 1760 AD between the French, under the Comte de Lally and the British, under Sir Eyre Coote. The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764 AD between British East India Company under Hector Munro and the combined armies of Mir Kasim, Nawab of Awadh, Shuja-ud-Daula and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam-II.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S. 2005 · Modern India GS p.369

subject: AP & Indian History
question: In 19th century, the fear of extension towards India of which country was the basis of Anglo- Afghan relations?
explanation: During the 19th century, the problem of Indo- Afghan relations got inextricably mixed up with the Anglo-Russian rivalry. Britain was expanding colonial power in West, South, and East Asia, Russia was an expanding power in Central Asia and desired to extend its territorial control in West and East Asia. Throughout the 19th century, the British rulers of India feared that Russia would launch an attack on India through Afghanistan and the North Western frontier of India. They, therefore, wanted to keep Russia at a safe distance from the Indian frontier. It was the basis of Anglo-Afghan relations.
source: UPPCS Spl. (Mains) G.S. 2004 · Modern India GS p.374

explanation: The first film advertisement in India appeared on July 7, 1896 when a Times of India advertisement invited the Bombay residents to witness “The Marvel of the century, the wonder of the world" at Watson’s Hotel. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Which one of the following Indian leaders was dismissed by the British from the Indian Civil Service?
explanation: After graduating from the University of Calcutta in 1868, Surendranath Banerjee travelled to England along with Ramesh Chunder Dutt and Behari Lal Gupta to compete in the Indian Civil Service examinations. He cleared the competitive examination in 1869, but was barred owing to a claim he had misrepresented about his age. After clearing the matter in the courts by arguing that he calculated his age according to the Hindu custom of reckoning age from the date of conception rather than from birth, Banerjee cleared the exam again in 1871 and was posted as Assistant Magistrate in Sylhet.

K. Halder, K. N. Majumdar, S. N. Gupta and a host of others. The first major exponent of Swadeshi values in Indian art, he is known to have founded the Bengal School of Art Neo-Bengal School. He was also a noted writer and known as ‘Aban Thakur’. His paintings are classified as revivalistic.

He founded the Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha (university) along with C. Rajagopalachari in hopes of spreading the learning of Hindi across the country. Due to his devotion, he was elected the chief of the Jaipur Rajya Praja Mandal in 1938. In honour of his social initiatives the Jamnalal Bajaj Award has been instituted by the Bajaj Foundation. He was awarded Padma Bhushan in 1967. He died in 1983.

question: Which of the following was advocated by Nehru but not by Gandhiji?
options: Heavy industrialization History of Modern India
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was the most outspoken advocate of industrialization in the early years of Indian independence. An ardent believer in modern science and socialism, he believed that industrialization held the key to India’s success as an independent nation. In promoting industrialization, Nehru departed from the course taken by his predecessor, Mahatma Gandhi. In Gandhi’s vision for independent India, the village would serve as the basis for Indian life. Indian society would have none of the dehumanizing bigness of industrialization. He advocated for handloom and small scale industries. Nehru disagreed with the central tenets of Gandhian economics.

subject: AP & Indian History
question: Who was the first Indian to go to jail while discharging the duty of journalist?
explanation: Surendranath Banerjee one of the founding fathers of the national movement, became the first Indian to go to jail in performance of his duty as a journalist. A dispute concerning a family idol called ‘Saligram’ had come up before Justice Norris of the Calcutta High Court. To decide the age of the idol, Norris ordered it to be brought to the Court and pronounced that it could not be a hundred years old. This Action deeply hurt the sentiments of the Bengali Hindus. Banerjee wrote an angry editorial in the ‘Bengalee’ of April 2, 1883. Comparing Norris with the notorious Jeffreys and Seroggs (British judges in the 17th century, notorious for infamous conduct as judges), he said that Norris had done enough ‘to show how unworthy he is of his high office.’ Immediately, the High Court hauled him up for contempt of court before a bench of five judges, four of them Europeans. With the Indian judge, Romesh Chandra Mitra, dissenting, the bench convicted and sentenced him to two months imprisonment.

explanation: In the general elections of February, 1977 the Janta Party had captured 330 out of 542 seats and Morarji Desai became the Prime Minister of India on March 23, 1977. Singh fell down and on November 10, 1990 Chandreshekhar Rao became the Prime Minister with the outer support of Congress. subject: AP & Indian History
question: Consider the following statements about Madam Bhikaji Cama : 1. Madam Cama unfurled the National Flag at the international Socialist Conference in Paris in the year 1907. 2. Madam Cama served as private secretary to Dadabhai Naoroji. 3. Madam Cama was born to Parsi parents. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Bhikaji Cama was born to Sorabji Framji Patel and Jaijibai Patel on September 24, 1861 at Bombay. She belonged to an affluent Gujarati-speaking Parsi family. In 1907 while attending Socialist Congress at Stuttgart (Germany) Madam Bhikaji Cama unfurled the first Indian national flag designed by her. This flag was the precursor of the flag of Independent India. The only difference that came later was the use of red instead of orange. Hence statement (1) is incorrect. In London, she came in touch with several Indian independence activists such as Shyamji Krishna Verma, Dadabhai Naoroji and Singh Rewabhai Rana. She started working as private secretary of Dadabhai Naoroji.

explanation: Born in May 18, 1853 in Baroda (present day Vadodara) Berahamji M. Malabari was a social reformer and the chief crusader for the Age of Consent Act, 1891 who campaigned all his life against child marriage and “enforced widowhood”. He founded the Seva Sadan as a social reform and humanitarian organization in 1885. His life work began in 1880 when he acquired the Indian Spectator, an English language daily which he edited for twenty years until it was merged into the Voice of India, which Malabari had already been editing together with Dadabhai Naoroji and William Wedderburn since 1883. In 1901 he became editor of the monthly ‘East and West’, a position he held until shortly before his death on July 12, 1912 at Shimla.

question: Statement I: Nationalism in India, which was assigned a privileged position by its western educated political leadership, was a different', but a derivative discourse from the west. Statement II : Indian nationalism as a response to western imperialism was “like all such responses, shaped by what it was responding to”.
options: Both the statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement I
Both the statements are individually true but Statement II is NOT the correct explanation of Statement I
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
explanation: Nationalism in India, which was assigned a privileged position by its western educated political leadership, was a different but a derivative discourse from the west. In India, the origins of nationalism have been derived from the educated Indians from western countries. These nationalists were influenced by western education. Indian nationality was a different but evolved manifestation from the western world. Thus the first statement is true. Indian nationalism as a response to western imperialism was “like all such responses, shaped by what it was responding to”. Hence, both the statements are individually correct and statement II is correct explanation of statement I.

explanation: In India, the Privy Purse was a payment made to the ruling (royal or lower) families of erstwhile princely states as part of their agreements to first integrate with India in 1947 and later to merge their states in 1949 whereby they lost all ruling rights. The Privy Purse was continued to the royal families until the 26th Amendment in 1971 (Article-363-A), by which all their privileges and allowances from the Central Government ceased to exist, was implemented after a two-year legal battle. In some individual cases however, privy purses were continued for life for individuals who had held ruling powers before 1947.

explanation: The British government was keen to get Indian support for the Second World War.
